title: Mastering Cicatricial Ectropion: Pathophysiology & Management
summary: Cicatricial ectropion represents a complex outward malposition of the eyelid margin caused by shortening of the anterior lamella. Precision in diagnosis and early surgical intervention are paramount to preventing chronic ocular surface disease.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Cicatricial ectropion is a structural malposition where the eyelid margin turns outward, away from the globe, due to vertical cicatricial contraction of the anterior lamella (skin and orbicularis oculi). This results in exposure keratopathy, chronic epiphora, and conjunctival keratinization.

sections.title: Etiology: Causes of Cicatricial Ectropion
content: Mechanical Trauma: Full-thickness skin loss
Thermal/Chemical Burns
Chronic Actinic Damage: Solar elastosis
Dermatologic Conditions: Ichthyosis, Pemphigoid, SJS/TEN
Post-Surgical: Over-aggressive blepharoplasty
Infectious: Zoster, Necrotizing fasciitis

rows: Inability to move tears to puncta

sections.title: Ocular Examination Protocol
content: Step 1: Snap-back and Distraction tests to assess horizontal laxity.
Step 2: Assess vertical eyelid height (measurement of vertical shortening).
Step 3: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy to grade corneal exposure/keratitis.
Step 4: Palpate for masses or subcutaneous scar tissue.
Step 5: Fluorescein staining for detection of exposure keratopathy.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Phase 1: Lubrication (PF-AT, gels, nocturnal ointment) to protect the cornea.
Phase 2: Surgical lysis of bands for mild cases.
Phase 3: Z-plasty or V-Y advancement flaps for localized scars.
Phase 4: Full-thickness skin graft (FTSG) for severe/extensive cicatricial loss.
Phase 5: Mid-lamellar lysis with spacers (e.g., hard palate graft) if posterior lamella is also involved.

sections.title: Red Flags for Urgent Referral
content: Corneal thinning or impending perforation
Severe exposure keratopathy unresponsive to maximal lubrication
Eyelid involvement from aggressive malignancy (e.g., BCC/SCC)
Evidence of orbital cellulitis or necrotizing process

content.explanation: L: Lysis of scar; I: Incise vertically; F: Full-thickness graft; T: Tension-free closure.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always evaluate for horizontal laxity; often, cicatricial ectropion requires a lateral tarsal strip concurrently.
Donors for skin grafts: Retroauricular skin is gold standard due to color/texture match.
If a patient has severe cicatricial ectropion, look for systemic mucous membrane pemphigoid.
